files.description: Burglar alarm bell (6-inch trembler gong in an outdoor bell box), heard a few metres away; nearly dry.
files.placement: 3D source on the shop facade above the fascia, min distance 2 m, max 60 m, Logarithmic rolloff; the key atmosphere element.

source.author: Jewelry-store-vr-demo project (generated with Claude, Anthropic)
source.changes: Modal synthesis: 12 split (doublet) gong modes + 22 weak inharmonic modes, trembler hammer at 18.6 strikes/s with timing/force jitter, contact damping, hammer bounce, armature buzz and rattle; bell-box cover EQ; short early reflections; rendered periodic (seamless); -20 LUFS; mono 16-bit WAV
source.reference: Mode ratios and levels measured from 'fire alarm bell' by msx2plus (freesound 678345, CC0) as mirrored in https://github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/VoxelGame/blob/1d0730642b44cd24182980a8da32b93b40dfc8ff/assets/sfx/alarm_loop.mp3 (sha256 2e3a37454e07172dc5acbb3ceb8eabf8c3918ab5150a23edcf5a9422295b5d86); no recorded audio used

source.changes: Upstream (350Chev): Freesound HQ preview, 5-28 s window time-warped to a steady 999 rpm, cut to whole engine cycles and looped, 96 kbps mono MP3. Here: MP3 decoded; DC removed; 45 Hz 4th-order high-pass (circular); the 3.60 s loop tiled 4x and read through a periodic time warp (+-0.6 % idle-speed hunting) with a +-0.7 dB periodic level drift, cubic interpolation; -20 LUFS (peak about -4.5 dBFS); mono 16-bit WAV. Replaces the first-release loop made from 'car idle' by seth-m (freesound 269771), which was 82 % sub-bass below 40 Hz.
